The university own capital project management office describes 12,000 square feet of network and data hall space plus supporting areas, at a total project budget of 72.75 million dollars. Construction began August 2024 with DLR Group as architect and McGough Construction as general contractor, with completion projected around August 2026. The project is intended to modernize and consolidate the university core network operations infrastructure, serving the university own IT and network operations rather than offering commercial colocation. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
The Advanced Operations Center is a 12,000 square foot data hall facility under construction at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities campus in Minneapolis, with a total project budget of 72.75 million dollars and completion projected for August 2026. The operator has published no critical IT megawatt figure for the facility, making it impossible to estimate rack or accelerator capacity from the specifications provided. The facility is designed to serve the university's own core network and IT operations rather than offer commercial colocation.

The published specifications do not identify any certifications for the facility. The university's project documentation does not state what technical capabilities the campus is built to host, so its fitness for any particular workload cannot be assessed from the data available.

Minnesota has 13 mapped data facilities, but only two operators in the state have published IT power specifications, totaling 10 megawatts. This campus ranks third in the state by published capacity, but that ranking reflects the absence of a published figure rather than a measured capacity. Without a power specification, this facility cannot be placed in the state's power landscape or assessed as a constraint on or asset to AI infrastructure scaling.
